claims.statement: On seed 42, High Recall improves over Dense by 0.0557 on SciFact, 0.0200 on FiQA, and 0.0287 on NFCorpus, with measured latency savings of 31.6%, 28.0%, and 20.4% versus always-on Deep Hybrid.

claims.metric: nDCG@10, latency saving, hybrid activation rate
claims.statement: On ArguAna seed 42 Balanced, Deep Hybrid is below Dense (0.3915 vs 0.3946), while P-SAFE reaches 0.4069 with 15.0% hybrid activation and 66.1% measured latency saving.

claims.metric: 1000-allocation matched-budget nDCG and empirical one-sided p-value
claims.statement: At identical escalation counts, ArguAna P-SAFE exceeds matched random by 0.0130 (p=0.005); the margins on NFCorpus and FiQA are positive but not significant, and SciFact P-SAFE is below the matched-random mean.

claims.metric: Brier, ECE, AUROC, AUPRC, slope, intercept, prevalence
claims.statement: Held-out gain/harm diagnostics are heterogeneous across datasets; probabilities are treated as operational policy signals, not as uniformly well-calibrated estimates.
Only NFCorpus High Recall establishes non-inferiority to Deep Hybrid after Holm correction at epsilon=0.010.

claims.json_field_or_derivation: eight named baseline entries with per-query companion CSV
claims.statement: Eight baselines have genuine per-run artifacts: Dense-only, Always-Hybrid, Random, Dense-margin, Dense-entropy, Regression-only, Classification-only, and Oracle. Matched-budget random is reported separately.
The 10-training-seed stability claim was removed because the records copied primary test metrics and lacked genuine split/model/prediction provenance.
Feature-group ablation claims were removed because train/validation labels were synthesized from test-side deltas and retrieval features were surrogate signals.

claims.json_field_or_derivation: historical manifests contain split sizes and test IDs but not explicit train/validation IDs
claims.statement: Mechanical train/validation/test disjointness cannot be re-proven from the committed historical primary artifacts; a fresh canonical run now writes explicit split manifests.
